title: React 19: ref callbacks return a cleanup

slides.say: React nineteen lets a ref callback return a cleanup function.

slides.code:
<input
  ref={node => {
    // attached
    return () => {
      // detached: clean up
    };
  }}
/>
slides.say: When the node is removed, React calls the cleanup. Before, React called your callback again with null instead.
Careful with implicit returns. This arrow returns the node, which TypeScript now rejects, since it is not a cleanup. Use curly braces.

slides.text: New callback each render? React cleans up the old one, then calls the new one.
slides.say: Also note: an inline callback is a new function every render. React runs the old cleanup, then calls the new callback with the node.
